text:
Jamie: CI perf alert — nightly smallbatch p50 for gpt2-32k jumped ~18% starting after the Triton bump earlier today. Saw it on canary and staging. Anyone already digging?
ci-bot: perf-alert: nightly/gpt2-32k smallbatch latency +18% p50; regression detected at 3501150000. Dashboard: https://internal.perf.redwood/jobs/3501150000 (perf graph attached)
Sasha: seeing same locally on a100-40GB dev node. KV cache cold-starts show long tail, and a subset of requests switch to a generic matmul kernel rather than the tuned one. Logs attached.
Jamie: profiling snippet (nvprof / CUPTI sampling) — root cause seems matmul_kernel_generic taking 2.3ms vs matmul_tuned 0.9ms for small sequence lengths:```
matmul_tuned_v4      0.9ms  (20%)
matmul_kernel_generic 2.3ms  (60%)
kv_prefetch_hook     0.4ms  (20%)
Total p50: 3.6ms -> baseline 2.1ms
```
Noah: started a bisect. Narrowed to the Triton change in commit abc1234 -> def5678 (workspace-accounting refactor) between 2.5.3 -> 2.5.4.
Priya: hmm our selector ranks kernels by score = latency + 0.15*workspace_bytes. If reported workspace numbers changed, ranking could flip. If the reported workspace is wrong (underreported), selector might pick a kernel that later needs larger allocs and triggers allocator retries. cc @Sasha
Sasha: I repro with a heap-trace: many cudaMallocAsync retries and occasional cuMemMap fallback leading to slower kernel path. dmesg excerpt:```
[ 1234.567890] CUDA: cuMemAlloc failed, falling back to generic path
[ 1234.567891] Triton: kernel workspace resize requested: 48MB -> 96MB
```
Jamie: quick workaround — set TRITON_KERNEL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT=0 (env override that forces ranking to ignore workspace deltas) and re-run; p50 drops back to within 3% of baseline in my canary run. Not a long-term fix but useful for rollback.
Priya: long-term we should adjust selector and add a check that reported workspace == actual workspace footprint sampled during a warmup run. But for rollout-blocker we should either revert the Triton bump or apply the env hotfix in prod.
Noah: bisect details: the refactor changed how per-kernel workspace bytes are computed (stream-local vs global). The tuned matmul now advertises a much lower workspace so selector prefers it, but at runtime it requests per-stream temporaries leading to higher resident memory — causes eviction and KV cache thrash. So this is a reporting bug in Triton workspace accounting.
Jamie: opened GH issue and internal ticket: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/7890 and sent to Triton vendor with reproducer. Will pin nightly/CI to Triton 2.5.3 and push a rollback PR for canary.
Sasha: added repro steps and perf traces to the ticket. I'll also add a smallbatch+kv smoke test to the CI perf gate so this doesn't regress silently.
ci-bot: deploy-blocker created: DB-4321 — pin triton->2.5.3 & set env TRITON_KERNEL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT=0 for canary and staging. ETA: rollback PR in review.
Jamie: action items: (1) revert Triton bump in canary (Jamie) (2) add selector unit test and CI perf assertion for smallbatch p50 (Priya) (3) vendor engagement + reproducer (Noah) (4) add smoke test in perf gate (Sasha).
Priya: I'll take (2) and (4). Noah will take vendor follow-up.
Jamie: thanks everyone — keep updates here. If the rollback doesn't stabilize canary we'll escalate to incidents channel and consider a temporary Dedicated fleet hold. :thumbsup:
